messages:
jonah: Heads-up — nightly perf job blew up after the merge that landed the new kernel heuristic. 22% token/sec regression on small-batch (batch_size=1..4) workloads. compile tasks spiked and GPU utilization is all over the place.

sophia: Ugh. Which commit/PR? any obvious logs?

jonah: PR  #789 (autotune: prefer f32-win32 kernels for throughput) — seems to have changed pick order. root cause looks like it picks a kernel that compiles slow & produces larger l2 usage on p4. CI trace: compile storm ~ 120 compilations in 10m.

perf-bot: nightly/perf-small-batch - job failed threshold: -22% throughput vs baseline. profiler snapshot attached in job artifacts (link).

maria: Could this be interacting with KV cache invalidation? small-batch path hits prefix-cache more, but if kernel changes key layout invalidation churn could spike compile/cache misses.

alex: If it's picking a different kernel variant, we should be able to repro locally: run the perf harness with --force-autotune=on and collect kernel pick logs. jonah can you paste the pick trace?

jonah: pastebin of pick trace (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] pick_kernel() chosen=kernel_v2_win32_f32 score=0.87 heuristic=latency_weighted
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] compile(kernel_v2_win32_f32) start
[2026-03-17 02:12:18] compile(...) end status=ok compile_time_ms=7060
[2026-03-17 02:12:18] fallback_check -> false (fallback disabled for 'dedicated' tier)
[2026-03-17 02:12:19] dispatch -> cache_miss, kv_cache_invalidate(reason=kernel_variant_change)
[2026-03-17 02:12:19] queue length spikes -> batching heuristic switches to small-batch path
```

jonah: repro command I ran: `tools/perf/harness --profile small-batch --model llama-3-mini --runs 100 --dump-kernel-choices` returns consistent pick of kernel_v2_win32_f32 on our p4 ci image.

sophia: Interesting that fallback is disabled for dedicated tier — we probably want a safety net during rollout. Was that change intentional in the PR?

alex: PR diff shows the commit toggled prefer_f32 for kernels when sequence_len > 512, but autotune decision tree has params for batch distribution which we didn't update. small-batch ended up meeting the metric to prefer f32 kernels because the estimator mis-weighted compile_cost.

maria: Also seeing more KV cache invalidation in the traces (artifact lines): `kv_cache.invalidate keys=7 reason=kernel_variant_change`. That will blow up latency for chat workloads that rely on KV reuse.

ci-bot: rerun requested by @sophia: buildkite #2045 requeued -> running.

perf-bot: quick profile diff (hotspots):
- kernel_compile ~ +6.0s per unique kernel compile
- l2-cache-miss-rate +14% on token-loop

jonah: Bisect attempt: rolled up to commit 3f2b1 (pre-PR) perf baseline restored. Narrowed to the autotune heuristics commit 7a9d4.

sophia: ok let's not revert the whole PR yet. Proposal: temporary change to force previous kernel preference for batch_size<=4 OR re-enable fallback so that if compile_time > threshold we pick an already-compiled variant. Which is safer for rollout?

alex: Re-enabling fallback is fastest. Small patch: if compile_time_estimate > 2000ms or expected_compile_qps > 0.1, pick compiled_variant or use cached variant. I can draft and cut a hotfix PR.

maria: Also add a metric to alert on kv_cache.invalidate rate spikes so we can catch this earlier.

jonah: +1 to both. I'll open a rollback PR for the autotune change (just revert 7a9d4) to unblock the rollout, and alex you can put the fallback patch as follow-up.

deploy-bot: rollout status: paused on version v2026.3.17 after perf regression detected. No further canary pushes.

alex: Drafted quick revert PR -> #796. Will include test that simulates small-batch distro and asserts kernel pick doesn't flip to f32-win32 in current hw profile.

sophia: Thanks. Action items: jonah revert PR (hotfix), alex add fallback + unit test, maria add kv_cache invalidate alert, perf-bot to add nightly guard for small-batch throughput. We'll re-run CI after revert and confirm compile counts drop.

jonah: I'll open the revert now and tag @eng-runtime. Thanks team :thumbsup:
